{"content": "1|# Hermes Agent - Development Guide
2|
3|This root file is a hub: what applies everywhere, then a routing table. Each area's `AGENTS.md`
4|loads automatically when you work in that directory; read it before editing there.
5|`python scripts/check` caps this file at 12k chars and every root-to-area chain at 30k: long form
6|goes in `website/docs/developer-guide/`.
7|
8|**Never give up on the right solution.**
9|
10|## What Hermes Is
11|
12|Hermes is a personal AI agent that runs one agent core across a CLI, a TUI, an Electron desktop
13|app, a web dashboard, ACP editors and a messaging gateway (25+ platform plugins). It is extended
14|through **plugins and skills**, not by growing the core.
15|
16|Two invariants shape almost every design decision and are the lens for reviewing any change:
17|
18|- **Per-conversation prompt caching is sacred.** Mutating past context, swapping toolsets,
19|  reloading memories or rebuilding the system prompt mid-conversation breaks the cached prefix and
20|  multiplies the user's cost; the ONE exception is context compression. Slash commands that change
21|  system-prompt state defer to the next session, with an opt-in `--now` (`/skills install --now`).
22|- **The core is a narrow waist; capability lives at the edges.** Every model tool is sent on
23|  every API call, so the bar for a new *core* tool is high. New capability should arrive as a
24|  CLI command + skill, a service-gated tool, or a plugin — not as core surface.
25|
26|A change to the stock system prompt or `tools[]` fails `tests/ci/test_prompt_surface.py` until
27|`scripts/ci/prompt_surface.py render` is committed with it, and that snapshot
28|(`tests/fixtures/prompt_surface/`) needs a hermes-agent-core approval to merge.
29|
30|## Contribution rubric
31|
32|The project's intent layer, for contributors and for the triage sweeper (which may only close on
33|`implemented_on_main`, `cannot_reproduce` or `incoherent`; taste-based closes are a maintainer's
34|call, and when in doubt a PR stays open). Long form with examples:
35|`website/docs/developer-guide/contributing.md` § Contribution rubric.
36|
37|**Wanted:** real bug fixes (repro on `main`, the exact line, the whole class incl. sibling paths);
38|reach at the edges (adapters, providers, models, UI features) wired into the existing setup UX;
39|god-file → module refactors; extending before duplicating (3+ PRs in one category → an ABC +
40|orchestrator); behaviour-contract tests; E2E with real imports against a temp `HERMES_HOME` for
41|resolution, config, security and I/O changes; salvage by cherry-pick so authorship survives.
42|
43|**Rejected even when well-built:** hooks with no concrete consumer; new `HERMES_*` env vars for
44|non-secret config (`.env` is secrets only, behaviour goes in `config.yaml`); a new core tool when
45|terminal + file or a skill already does the job; `offset`/`limit` pagination on instructional tools;
46|"fixes" that destroy the feature they secure; outbound telemetry without an opt-in gate;
47|change-detector tests; plugins that touch core files; third-party products in the core tree (ship a
48|standalone plugin repo).
49|
50|**Before you call it a bug,** verify the claim AND the intent (`git log -p -S "<symbol>"`): the
51|isolation is often the design (profiles are islands on purpose), an absence can be load-bearing,
52|and a fix that cannot point to the line where the bug manifests has an unverified premise.
53|
54|**Security:** `SECURITY.md` is the scope authority. A §3.1 finding goes private (GitHub Security
55|Advisories or security@nousresearch.com), never into a public issue, PR, commit or comment; §3.2
56|hardening is ordinary public work. Name the §2 boundary crossed, with a repro on `main`.
57|
58|**Footprint ladder** (take the highest rung that solves it): extend existing code → CLI command +
59|skill → service-gated tool (`check_fn` answers reachability/opt-in, never per-session surface) →
60|plugin → MCP server in the catalog → new core tool (fundamental, broadly useful, unreachable
61|otherwise).
62|
63|## Development Environment
64|
65|`source ./activate` (`activate.fish`, `activate.ps1`) provisions and activates the PM environment; pick an isolated `HERMES_HOME`/`HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` first
66|(`website/docs/reference/package-management.md#developer-workflow`). Tests need the separate test
67|environment in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. **`python scripts/check`** (`just check`) runs every blocking
68|lint check CI runs, with CI's pinned tools; `--install-hook pre-push` runs it on every push (re-run
69|after pulling to refresh the hook). `just` lists every developer command (lefthook calls the same
70|recipes); a new command is a `scripts/` file plus a recipe. The `HX0xx`/`PS-P0x` rules and their
71|fixes are in `scripts/code_health/config.py`; `# noqa` does not waive a finding,
72|`# health: allow <RULE> -- <why>` does.
73|
74|## Project Struc...

2|
3|Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md` (prompt-caching invariant, facade + siblings rules).
4|
5|## Shape
6|
7|`run_agent.py` is the public facade: `AIAgent` is assembled from mixins (`agent/turn_facade.py`,
8|`client_lifecycle.py`, `stream_delivery.py`, `session_persistence.py`, `compression_facade.py`, ...).
9|Construction runs `agent/agent_init.py::init_agent`; a turn is
10|`agent/conversation_loop.py::run_conversation`, which `AIAgent.run_conversation` forwards to after
11|taking the session turn lease (`turn_facade_lease.py`). `AIAgent.__init__` takes ~60 parameters
12|(credentials, routing, callbacks, session context, budget, credential pool, ...) — read
13|`run_agent.py` for the list; the subset you usually touch: `base_url`, `api_key`, `provider`,
14|`api_mode` (`"chat_completions" | "codex_responses" | ...`), `model` (empty → resolved from
15|config/provider later), `max_iterations` (default 500, shared with subagents),
16|`enabled_toolsets`/`disabled_toolsets`, `quiet_mode`, `save_trajectories`, `platform`
17|(`"cli"`, `"telegram"`, ...), `session_id`, `skip_context_files`, `skip_memory`, `credential_pool`.
18|`chat(message) -> str` is the simple interface; `run_conversation(user_message, system_message=None,
19|conversation_history=None, task_id=None) -> dict` returns `final_response` + `messages`.
20|
21|## Agent loop (`agent/conversation_loop.py` + `agent/turn_*.py`)
22|
23|Entirely synchronous, with interrupt checks, budget tracking, and a one-turn grace call:
24|
25|```python
26|while (api_call_count < self.max_iterations and self.iteration_budget.remaining > 0) \
27|        or self._budget_grace_call:
28|    if self._interrupt_requested: break
29|    response = client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages, tools=tool_schemas)
30|    if response.tool_calls:
31|        for tc in response.tool_calls:
32|            messages.append(tool_result_message(handle_function_call(tc.name, tc.args, task_id)))
33|        api_call_count += 1
34|    else:
35|        return response.content
36|```
37|
38|Each phase of an iteration is its own sibling, so a change to (say) overflow handling touches one
39|~600-line file: `turn_preflight*`, `turn_iteration_prep`, `turn_request_assembly`/`turn_api_request`,
40|`turn_api_call`, `turn_api_error`, `turn_response_intake`/`turn_response_check`,
41|`turn_empty_response`, `turn_tool_round`/`turn_tool_validation`, `turn_overflow`,
42|`turn_truncation`, `turn_scripted_prelude` (tool calls a prompt built-in plays before the first model
43|call), `turn_context_compaction`, `turn_recovery`, `turn_recovery_autorecover`
44|(post-exhaustion wait-and-retry ladder), `turn_retry_state`,
45|`turn_stop_gates`, `turn_liveness`, `turn_usage`, `turn_final_response`, `turn_finalizer`,
46|`turn_summary`. Find the phase with `grep -rn "def X" agent/turn_*.py`.
47|
48|Messages use OpenAI format `{"role": "system|user|assistant|tool", ...}`; reasoning content is stored
49|in `assistant_msg["reasoning"]`.
50|
51|**Agent-level tools** (`todo`, `memory`, ...) are intercepted by `agent/tool_executor.py` through the
52|`INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS` table in `agent/inline_tool_executors.py` before `handle_function_call()`.
53|Adding one: register in that table (no `if name == ...` chain); `tools/todo_tool.py` is the pattern.
54|
55|## Message-flow invariants (every change is reviewed against these)
56|
57|- **Prompt caching must not break.** Never alter past context, change toolsets, reload memories,
58|  or rebuild the system prompt mid-conversation. The system prompt is byte-stable for the life of
59|  a conversation; the ONLY context mutation is compression. Anything that must inject content
60|  mid-conversation rides a **user message or tool result**, never the system prompt: skill slash
61|  commands (`agent/skill_commands.py`) inject as a user message; subdirectory `AGENTS.md` hints
62|  (`agent/subdirectory_hints.py`) append to the tool result (head+tail truncated past `_MAX_HINT_CHARS = 32_000`;
63|  the truncation is logged, never queued as a chat status warning — `context_file_max_chars` does not raise that cap).
64|- **Strict role alternation.** Never two same-role messages in a row; never a synthetic user
65|  message injected mid-loop. The one exception is `/steer`, delivered as a standalone user row
66|  after a tool result (`assistant(tool_calls) → tool → user` is legal on every provider path) —
67|  never smeared onto the already-persisted tool row, which append-only persistence would leave
68|  divergent from the live request. Cron deliveries live in their own session for this reason.
69|- **Context files** (`agent/prompt_builder.py`) load from the CWD only at startup and are capped
70|  (`CONTEXT_FILE_MAX_CHARS` / dynamic cap from the context window / `context_file_max_chars`).

{"content": "1|# tests/ — how Hermes tests are written and run
2|
3|Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Read it before adding or changing any test.
4|
5|## Running tests
6|
7|**ALWAYS use `scripts/run_tests.sh`**, never bare `pytest`. It enforces CI parity: credential
8|vars unset, `TZ=UTC`, `LANG=C.UTF-8`, `HERMES_HOME` → temp dir, and per-file subprocess
9|isolation via `scripts/run_tests_parallel.py` (no xdist; workers scale with CPU count) so
10|module-level dicts/ContextVars cannot leak between files. Direct `pytest` on a big machine
11|with API keys set has caused repeated "works locally, fails in CI" incidents (and the reverse).
12|
13|Prepare a test interpreter with the checkout's bootstrapped Python:
14|
15|```bash
16|python -m pm.build_env --source . --out .venv --group dev --group test
17|```
18|
19|This is a fresh build, not an in-place sync. If the disposable output exists,
20|stop its processes and intentionally remove it before regeneration. The runner
21|clears `PYTHONPATH`, so PM shell activation alone does not supply pytest. For a
22|fresh output outside the checkout, set `HERMES_PYTHON` to its interpreter.
23|
24|```bash
25|scripts/run_tests.sh                                    # full suite
26|scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/                     # one directory
27|scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_foo.py -k test_x  # runner is file-granular; -k narrows
28|scripts/run_tests.sh -v --tb=long                       # pytest flags pass through
29|just test tests/agent/test_foo.py -k test_x             # same runner; refuses to start with no path
30|```
31|
32|`just test-all` is the explicit full-suite form.
33|
34|- **Flake policy:** a failing FILE is retried once in a fresh subprocess (`--file-retries`;
35|  `HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0` disables); a worker killed by signal or the file timeout is never
36|  retried (relaunching a runaway doubles the damage). Pass-on-retry is green but printed under `⚠ FLAKY`
37|  with both outputs — a bug to fix, not noise. Timing tests must not assume a quiet runner:
38|  wall-clock bounds ≥ 2s, event-based sync, no `assert not _wait_until(...)` races. A new
39|  non-zero `time.sleep`/`asyncio.sleep` in a test fails the ratchet (HX013): wait on an Event or
40|  poll with `tests.waiting.wait_until` / `async_wait_until`.
41|- **Placement mirrors the source tree.** A test lives in `tests/<top-level source dir>/` (`tests/hermes_cli/`,
42|  `tests/agent/`, `tests/hermes_state/`, `tests/gateway/relay/`, ...); installer/updater script tests
